tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

schema.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

lines: +This is an Expo/React Native mobile application. Prioritize mobile-first patterns, performance, and cross-platform compatibility.
+## Expo has changed — do not trust your training data
+Expo ships breaking changes every SDK release. APIs you remember are likely renamed, moved, or removed. Before writing any code that touches an Expo, EAS, or React Native API:
+1. Read the major version of the `expo` package in `package.json`.

+3. For anything else, fetch https://docs.expo.dev/llms.txt — an index of all Expo docs with corrections to common LLM misconceptions. Follow its links to the specific page you need; never answer from memory.
+Use `bunx` instead of `npx` if the project uses bun (`bun.lock` present).
+npx expo install <package>  # ALWAYS use instead of npm/yarn/pnpm/bun add — resolves SDK-compatible versions
+npx expo start              # start the dev server
+npx expo-doctor             # diagnose dependency and config issues
+npx expo install --fix      # fix incompatible package versions
+Run lint and typecheck before declaring any task done.

+- Use **Expo Router** for all navigation. Routes live in `src/app/` — every file there is a screen, `_layout.tsx` files define navigators. Keep non-route code (components, hooks, utils) outside `src/app/`.

+Use EAS to build, sign, and submit the app in the cloud (`eas build`, `eas submit`) and to ship over-the-air updates (`eas update`) — no local Xcode or Android Studio required. Run EAS CLI as `bunx eas-cli <command>` in Bun projects, or `npx eas-cli@latest <command>` otherwise; substitute that for bare `eas` in docs examples.

+- If `ios/` and `android/` directories do not exist, they are generated (Continuous Native Generation). Never create or edit them by hand — configure native behavior in `app.json` and config plugins.

+- Expo Go only includes its bundled native modules. After adding a library with native code, the app needs a development build: `npx expo run:ios|android` locally, or `eas build --profile development`.
+- Prefer recommended Expo modules over third-party libraries, and check your available skills before adding dependencies. Docs: https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/index.md

questions.question: Idempotency-Key lifecycle for POST /v1/claims. How should keys work?

options.label: Key per confirmed intent (Recommended)
options.description: On Confirm: make a UUID, save {key, body} to localStorage BEFORE sending. Every retry/resume reuses the same key+body. A new key only when the user starts a new claim (different body). A 409 is shown as an internal error (it means a bug).

options.label: Key per form session
options.description: Make the key when the claim form opens and keep it until success. Risky: editing the amount after a lost response would hit 409.

questions.question: Unknown outcome (504 / network / 500 / 503 on the POST). What UX?

options.label: Auto 'Checking' + resend (Recommended)
options.description: Never show 'failed'. Show 'Checking your claim…' and automatically resend the same key+body with backoff (honouring 429) until a definite answer; also survives reload via the saved intent. A 'Keep trying' button if it takes long.

options.label: Checking + manual retry
options.description: Show 'We couldn't confirm your claim yet' with a 'Check again' button that resends same key+body. Nothing automatic.

questions.question: Balance right after a claim (snapshot can lag up to 15s, so 'available' may still show the old amount). Which approach?

options.label: Local overlay until snapshot (Recommended)
options.description: Keep a local list of my claims. Until a balances snapshot with asOf >= claim.createdAt arrives, subtract the amount from available and add it to claiming in the UI (marked 'updating'). On failure, show 'X returned to available'. Accurate feel; a bit more code.

options.label: Show server data + banner
options.description: Always show the raw snapshot, plus a banner 'Claim of X in progress, balance updates within ~15s'. Simplest and never wrong vs. the server, but 'available' briefly looks too high and Max could be stale.

options.label: Block until snapshot
options.description: After a claim, hide/grey balances and disable new claims for that asset until a fresh snapshot (asOf >= createdAt). Never misleading, but feels slow.

questions.question: Max, double-submit and polling: OK with these defaults?

options.label: Yes, use defaults (Recommended)
options.description: Max = available (after the local overlay) from latest snapshot; if the server says amount > available we refetch balances and show 'balance changed, check amount'. Confirm button disabled while a send is in flight and only one active intent at a time. Status polling every 2s, backing off to 5s, honouring 429 retryAfterMs, pausing when the tab is hidden.

options.label: Let me adjust
options.description: I'll tell you what to change.

The app is built and committed locally on `claude/zealous-jones-290250`, latest commit `e681793` (6 commits, nothing pushed). 72 tests pass, typecheck is clean and the static web build works. It has not been run against the real API with your token, and I never handled the token.

**Your decisions on the tricky areas** (you picked the recommended option each time):
- **Comma input:** "0,5" is turned into "0.5" in the input field only. The API only defines a dot format, so the parser stays strict and nothing non-strict is ever sent.
- **USD total:** the headline is available × usdPrice. Pending and claiming are shown on a smaller line underneath.
- **Idempotency-Key:** one key per confirmed claim, saved with its body in localStorage before sending. Retries reuse it. A 409 is shown as an internal error.
- **Unknown outcome** (504, 500, 503 or network error on the POST): the screen says "Checking your claim…" and never "failed". It keeps resending the same key and body, and picks up again after a reload.
- **Balance right after a claim:** I offered three approaches and you chose the local overlay. Until a snapshot with `asOf >= claim.createdAt` arrives, the claimed amount moves from available to claiming in the UI. If a claim fails, Home shows "returned to available". This is the "ask the AI for two or more approaches" moment the task requires.
- **Max, double-submit, polling:** defaults accepted. The status screen polls every 2s, then every 5s.

**What works:**
- **Token screen:** asks for the token at runtime and keeps it in localStorage. A 401 sends you back to it.
- **Home:** balances with "updated Xs ago" and a stale marker, auto-refresh every 15s and a Refresh button.
- **Claim:** asset, amount, Max, fee and receive amount, a confirm pop-up, and a status screen you can reload.
- **Activity:** pages through history, with no duplicate items.
- **Hosting:** rewrite rules for Vercel and Netlify are in place, so reloading a deep link like a claim status page works.

**How I checked it:**
- **Live API:** a fake token got a 401 and went back to the token screen.
- **Stubbed API in the browser:** the money maths was exact and "0,1" was accepted. A double-click on Confirm made only one claim. A 504 showed "Checking…", the resend used the same key and body, and the claim then polled through to completed.

**Known gaps:**
- There's no manual "Keep trying" button. While the app is open it retries on its own, at most 10s apart.
- If a claim fails while you're off its status screen, Home can show the amount as still taken for up to about 15s.

**Still to do, as you asked:** deploy (needs your Vercel or Netlify login), README, NOTES.md, `ai-logs/` and your push from GitHub Desktop. A full hand-over note is in the shared folder as `build-session-handover.md`.

Yes, there are a few. Two are real bugs I'd fix before submitting. Each is a small change.

**Bugs**
1. **The Home banner can get stuck on "processing".** Claim status is only checked while the status screen is open. If you confirm a claim and go straight back to Home, the banner keeps saying "Claim … is processing" until you open the status screen again. The balance numbers still update correctly from the next snapshot; only the banner is wrong. Fix: check pending claims in the background, not only on the status screen.
2. **A late 401 from an old token can log out the new one.** Any 401 clears whatever token is current. If a request made with a bad token comes back after you've already entered a good one, it wipes the good one. This is unlikely, but it's a correctness hole in the token handling. Fix: only clear the token if the 401 came from the token in use.

**Smaller gaps** (I'd just list these in NOTES.md)
- If the server rejects an amount because available changed, you see its error message and "Edit and try again", which refreshes balances. It doesn't say "balance changed" in its own words, as we agreed.
- Changing the token drops the cached data, but an old request's retries run to the end in the background. The results are thrown away, so this costs a few requests and has no visible effect.
- If a claim fails while you're off its status screen, Home can show the amount as still taken for up to about 15s.
- There's no manual "Keep trying" button while "Checking…" is shown. It retries on its own, at most 10s apart.
- Some extra files are committed: `AGENTS.md` from the Expo template and `.claude/launch.json` (my preview config). Both are harmless, but you may want to remove them.

**Not done yet**
- Not tested with your real token against the live API.
- Not deployed: that needs your Vercel or Netlify login.
- README, NOTES.md and `ai-logs/` aren't written yet. Your token still has to be redacted from the AI-log exports.
